findings.title: Firmware timezone split lacks render test
findings.why_it_matters: The device can regress to showing the spot's time for the last successful forecast while every current host test still passes. The web normalizer has a distinct-zone assertion, but the firmware's new device-versus-spot split is only present inside the static dashboard assembly path; renderer tests receive an already formatted update string and therefore cannot catch a swapped timezone. A small host-testable formatting seam with deliberately different device and spot zones would prove the behavior users actually see.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract the dashboard time-label preparation into a host-testable helper and add a test using one retrieval epoch with device timezone America/New_York and spot timezone Europe/Amsterdam; assert the update label is New York-local while the forecast date/hour labels remain Amsterdam-local, covering both 24-hour and 12-hour display modes.

residual_risks: The v2/v3 migration is covered through host-memory record sizing, but not with an ESP NVS blob fixture that proves the real nvs_get_blob size behavior.
The actual e-paper dashboard path is build-tested, but its rendered update label is not inspected in a host or screenshot test.
testing_gaps: No test verifies ConfiguratorView captures the browser timezone and passes it into the installation payload; configuration tests supply deviceTimezone directly.
No focused test covers deviceTimezone() returning Etc/UTC when Intl reports a missing or invalid timezone.
Installer rejection tests do not isolate a version-4 payload with a missing or unsupported deviceTimezone; their invalid fixtures are still version 2 and fail earlier.
Cache rejection tests use arbitrary incompatible versions rather than the exact previous version-3 envelope/schema-2 forecast being invalidated.
